summary: Sunapha forms when one or more planets other than the Sun occupy the 2nd sign from the Moon. The texts tie it mainly to self-earned wealth, intelligence and standing, coloured by whichever planet forms it.
common_outcomes: wealth and property gained by one's own effort (BPHS 37.7-10; Phaladeepika 6.6; Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 2)
intelligence, good reputation and a status 'equal to a king' in the classical idiom, meaning standing among one's own people (BPHS 37.7-10; Brihat Jataka 13.5)
learning in the sastras and a peaceable, virtuous disposition (Saravali 13.4)
rare_outcomes: Mars forming it: valour, wealth, harsh speech, command of soldiers, a fierce and proud nature (Saravali 13.10-11; Jataka Parijata 7.86 says a fierce, cruel, strong-minded ruler)
Mercury forming it: skill in Vedas, sastras, music and poetry, a brilliant physique (Saravali 13.10-11; Jataka Parijata 7.87)
Jupiter forming it: high learning, fame, a good family, plenty of wealth, favour of rulers (Saravali 13.12-14)
Venus forming it: wife, lands, wealth, cattle and honour from rulers (Saravali 13.12-14)
Saturn forming it: skill, respect in one's village or town, abundant wealth, devotion to work (Saravali 13.12-14)

by_area.personality: intelligent, virtuous, peaceable and well regarded (Saravali 13.4; BPHS 37.7-10)
by_area.career: rises by own effort to a position of authority; Saravali names king or minister in the classical idiom (Saravali 13.4)
by_area.finance: self-acquired property and wealth; Raman stresses that Sunapha has much influence on financial prosperity or adversity (Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 2, remarks)

strengtheners: benefic, well-placed or yogakaraka planets in the 2nd from the Moon (Raman no. 2: Venus as yogakaraka fortified finances in his chart 5)
several benefics in the 2nd from the Moon, e.g. Mercury, Jupiter and Venus together (Raman no. 2)
the 2nd from the Moon also falling in the 10th/11th from the lagna, which links the yoga to career and gains (Raman no. 2, Leo lagna illustration)
forming planets in exaltation, own or friendly signs or navamsas: then the full result is realised (Jataka Parijata 7.106)
a strong, bright Moon; the yoga works according to the Moon's state (Saravali 13.8-9)
the yoga operating in kendras: Saravali says one of royal birth then becomes a ruler (Saravali 35.176)
weakeners_or_cancellations: afflicted forming planets: Raman's chart 4 has five planets in the 2nd from the Moon with a debilitated Sun, Ketu and aspects of Saturn and Rahu, and he calls the yoga practically defunct (Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 2)
the Moon joined with Rahu or Ketu, Rahu in the 10th from the Moon, or a forming planet debilitated or combust: the results become mixed (Jataka Parijata 7.107)
lagna_or_context_notes: Raman notes that the houses the 2nd from the Moon occupies from the lagna shape the results; with Leo lagna and Taurus Moon, planets in Gemini connect the yoga to the 10th and 11th houses (Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 2).

source_views.source: BPHS 37.7-10 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1, ch. 'Lunar Yogas')
source_views.view: A planet other than the Sun in the 2nd from the Moon gives Sunapha; the native is a king or like one, intelligent, wealthy, famous, with self-earned wealth.
Same rule: a planet excluding the Sun in the 2nd from the Moon; the native becomes a king or equal to one.
Planets other than the Sun in the 2nd from the Moon give Sunapha; the native is a king or his equal, with self-acquired property, known for wisdom and wealth.

Excluding the Sun, any planet in the 2nd from the Moon; gives wealth, self-made position, learning, fame, rulership or ministry. Results depend on the Moon's phase, the forming planets' strength and the native's country and family. Separate results are given for Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus and Saturn.

Planets other than the Sun in the 2nd from the Moon; the native is a king or equal, with self-acquired property and renowned for wisdom. Sastri's note says planets in the 2nd from the Moon give accumulation of wealth. Varahamihira gives the per-planet results without separating 2nd from 12th.

Same definition; per-planet Sunapha results; full results when forming planets are exalted, in own or friendly signs or navamsas; mixed when the Moon is with a node, Rahu is 10th from the Moon, or the forming planet is debilitated or combust.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 2 Sunapha Yoga
source_views.view: Planets excepting the Sun in the 2nd from the Moon; self-earned property, intelligence, wealth, reputation. The nature of the yoga depends on the planets forming it; results come in the dasas and bhuktis of those planets; strongly tied to finances; can be rendered defunct by affliction.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XX 'Some Special Yogas', no. 10
source_views.view: Planets in the 2nd from the Moon: a self-made man with self-acquired wealth, intelligent and reputed.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, 11.3.1
source_views.view: Planets other than the Sun in the 2nd from the Moon; king or equal, intelligent, wealthy, famous, self-earned wealth.

disagreements: Varahamihira (Brihat Jataka 13.3, Sastri's notes) reports two minority methods that he rejects: Srutakirti counted planets in the 4th from the Moon for Sunapha, and Devasarma counted from the sign of the Moon's navamsa. Sastri adds a footnote that Parasara recognised these two views. Saravali 13.3 counts 30 varieties of Sunapha, while Brihat Jataka 13.4 and Raman count 31.
phrasing_guidance: Present this as a supportive yoga for earning by one's own effort. Name the planet forming it and its condition, since that changes the flavour a lot. Avoid promising wealth or rank; say it supports them when the forming planets are strong.

definitions.definition: A planet other than the Sun in the 2nd sign from the Moon.
Planets other than the Sun in the 2nd house from the Moon.
Excepting the Sun, any planet in the 2nd from the Moon.

Planets other than the Sun in the 2nd from the Moon; the commentary quoting Garga limits the planets to Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus and Saturn, so Rahu and Ketu are not counted. Positions are by sign, not bhava (note to 13.5).
The 2nd from the Moon occupied by planets other than the Sun.

definitions.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 2
definitions.definition: Planets, excepting the Sun, in the 2nd house from the Moon: Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus and Saturn, singly or together.

definitions.source: Brihat Jataka 13.3 (minority view of Srutakirti, rejected by Varahamihira)
definitions.definition: A planet other than the Sun in the 4th from the Moon.

cancellations.condition: Forming planet debilitated or combust, the Moon with Rahu or Ketu, or Rahu in the 10th from the Moon: results become mixed, not cancelled
Heavy affliction of the forming planets by malefics and nodes: the yoga is practically defunct
cancellations.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 2, chart 4

rarity_and_weight: Varahamihira counts 31 combinations of the five planets for Sunapha (Brihat Jataka 13.4; Raman no. 4 remarks); Saravali 13.3 says 30. The yoga is common because any of five planets will do. Raman weighs it by the nature and strength of the occupying planets and says it strongly influences finances (no. 2).
timing: Results show in the dasas and bhuktis of the planets that form the yoga (Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 2).

conditional_results.when: manual: if the planet in the 2nd from the Moon is exalted, in its own or a friendly sign, or in such a navamsa
manual: if the forming planet is debilitated or combust, or the Moon is with Rahu or Ketu, or Rahu is in the 10th from the Moon

summary: Anapha forms when one or more planets other than the Sun occupy the 12th sign from the Moon. The texts give good health and looks, character, fame and enjoyment, with spending rather than saving and, per Raman, detachment later in life.
common_outcomes: a healthy, well-formed body and a commanding appearance (BPHS 37.7-10; Raman no. 3)
virtue, fame and good manners (BPHS 37.7-10; Phaladeepika 6.6)
comforts, good dress, enjoyment of sense pleasures (Phaladeepika 6.6; Saravali 13.5)
rare_outcomes: renunciation and austerity in later life (Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 3; Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XX no. 9)
Mars forming it: leader of a band (Saravali says of thieves), arrogant, fond of war, honoured (Saravali 13.15-19)
Mercury forming it: skill in singing, dancing and writing, poet and orator, honoured by rulers (Saravali 13.15-19)
Jupiter forming it: majestic, intelligent, a poet, famous through a ruler (Saravali 13.15-19)
Venus forming it: strong liking for women, favour of rulers, abundant gold (Saravali 13.15-19)
Saturn forming it: broad-shouldered, a leader who keeps commitments, rich in cattle (Saravali 13.15-19)

by_area.personality: polite, generous, self-respecting, contented; eloquent per Saravali 13.5 (Raman no. 3; Phaladeepika 6.6)
by_area.finance: enjoyment and spending rather than accumulation; Sastri's note says planets in the 12th from the Moon give enjoyment without caring for accumulation (Brihat Jataka 13.5 note)
by_area.health: free from disease, well-formed limbs (BPHS 37.7-10; Phaladeepika 6.6; Raman no. 3)
by_area.spirituality: Raman links the 12th to moksha: the native cultivates detachment in later years (no. 3, chart 6)

strengtheners: strong, well-placed planets in the 12th from the Moon (Jataka Parijata 7.106)
a strong Moon (Saravali 13.8-9)
weakeners_or_cancellations: a debilitated forming planet weakens it; Raman calls the yoga 'feebly powerful' in chart 6 because Jupiter is debilitated, even with neecha bhanga (no. 3)
the Moon with Rahu or Ketu, Rahu in the 10th from the Moon, or a debilitated or combust forming planet: results mixed (Jataka Parijata 7.107)

source_views.view: A planet other than the Sun in the 12th from the Moon gives Anapha; the native is a king, free from disease, virtuous, famous, charming and happy.
Powerful, healthy, amiable, famous, comfortable, well dressed, contented and happy.

Excluding the Sun, a planet in the 12th from the Moon; eloquent, magnanimous, virtuous, enjoys food, drink, flowers, robes and women, famous, calm, beautiful body; separate results for each of the five planets.
Strong, healthy, amiable, famous, comfortable, well dressed, contented. The note says the 12th gives enjoyment rather than accumulation.
Same definition; general and per-planet Anapha results.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 3 Anapha Yoga
source_views.view: Planets in the 12th from the Moon (Sun not counted); well-formed organs, majestic appearance, reputation, politeness, generosity, fondness for dress and pleasures, and renunciation in later life. The Sunapha remarks apply with slight variation; each planet's share shows in its own dasa.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XX no. 9
source_views.view: Commanding appearance, health, morality, freedom from mental sorrow, renown, sense pleasures and later renunciation.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, 11.3.2
source_views.view: Planets other than the Sun in the 12th from the Moon; good looks, freedom from disease, character, reputation and comforts.

disagreements: Srutakirti (reported and rejected in Brihat Jataka 13.3 notes and Jataka Parijata 7.83 notes) took the 10th from the Moon for Anapha. Only Raman (and his Hindu Predictive Astrology) adds later-life renunciation; the classical verses read here do not mention it.
phrasing_guidance: Frame it as a yoga of health, presence and enjoyment, and note it leans toward spending. If Raman's detachment theme is used, offer it as a possible later-life inward turn, not a prediction of leaving home.

definitions.definition: A planet other than the Sun in the 12th sign from the Moon.
Planets other than the Sun in the 12th from the Moon.
Excepting the Sun, any planet in the 12th from the Moon.
Planets other than the Sun in the 12th from the Moon; per Garga only Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus and Saturn count.
The 12th from the Moon occupied by planets other than the Sun.

definitions.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 3
definitions.definition: Planets in the 12th from the Moon; the Sun is not taken into account.
A planet other than the Sun in the 10th from the Moon.

cancellations.condition: Forming planet debilitated or combust, the Moon with Rahu or Ketu, or Rahu in the 10th from the Moon: results mixed

rarity_and_weight: 31 varieties (Brihat Jataka 13.4; Raman no. 4 remarks); 30 in Saravali 13.3. Common; weighed by the strength of the occupying planets (Raman no. 3).
timing: Each forming planet gives its share of the yoga in its own dasa (Raman no. 3, chart 6, where Saturn's quota is expected in Saturn's dasa). Raman places the renunciation theme in later life.

conditional_results.when: manual: if the planet in the 12th from the Moon is exalted, in its own or a friendly sign, or in such a navamsa
manual: if the forming planet is debilitated or combust, or the Moon is with Rahu or Ketu, or Rahu is in the 10th from the Moon

summary: Durudhara (Dhurdhura) forms when planets other than the Sun occupy both the 2nd and the 12th signs from the Moon. It combines earning (2nd) with enjoying (12th): wealth, vehicles, generosity and comforts, coloured by the pair of planets involved.
common_outcomes: enjoyment of pleasures, wealth and vehicles (BPHS 37.7-10; Phaladeepika 6.7; Raman no. 4)
a charitable, bountiful nature (BPHS 37.7-10; Brihat Jataka 13.6; Raman no. 4)
faithful servants or attendants (BPHS 37.7-10; Phaladeepika 6.7)
rare_outcomes: grief from having to support family members (Saravali 13.6)
Mars and Mercury: untruthful, very wealthy, miserly, chief of his clan (Saravali 13.20)
Mars and Jupiter: famous for deeds, many enemies, protects his people, gathers money (Saravali 13.21)
Mars and Venus: a virtuous wife, fortunate, argumentative, fond of exercise, bold in war (Saravali 13.22)
Mars and Saturn: a difficult spouse, saves money, has vices, quick to anger, overcomes enemies (Saravali 13.23)
Jupiter and Mercury: learned, a poet, wealthy, famous (Saravali 13.24)
Mercury and Venus: sweet speech, fond of dance and music, a minister (Saravali 13.25)
Mercury and Saturn: travels from place to place to earn, little education, at odds with his own people (Saravali 13.26)
Jupiter and Venus: courageous, politically wise, owns gold and gems, in a ruler's service (Saravali 13.27)
Jupiter and Saturn: happy, politically knowledgeable, sweet-spoken, wealthy (Saravali 13.28)
Venus and Saturn: mature beyond his years, chief of his clan, dear to women, honoured, wealthy (Saravali 13.29; Jataka Parijata 7.105 gives a similar Venus-Saturn picture)

by_area.personality: liberal, generous, of good conduct; famed for speech, wisdom and valour (Saravali 13.6; Raman no. 4)
by_area.finance: both earns (planets in the 2nd) and spends or enjoys (planets in the 12th), per Sastri's note to Brihat Jataka 13.6; much wealth and conveyances (Raman no. 4)
by_area.relationships: spouse themes vary by pair: virtuous wife with Venus-Mars, a difficult one with Mars-Saturn (Saravali 13.22-23)
by_area.family: may come to grief through maintaining family members (Saravali 13.6)

strengtheners: well-dignified forming planets; Raman contrasts exalted Mars in the 2nd with Jupiter in the 12th against debilitated Jupiter in the 2nd with Mars in the 12th and says the permutations must be analysed (no. 4)
an exalted or strong Moon; Raman's chart 7 has the Moon exalted in Taurus with Saturn and Venus on either side (no. 4)
forming planets in exaltation, own or friendly signs or navamsas (Jataka Parijata 7.106)
weakeners_or_cancellations: the Moon with Rahu or Ketu, Rahu in the 10th from the Moon, or a debilitated or combust forming planet: mixed results (Jataka Parijata 7.107)
lagna_or_context_notes: Raman's chart 7: Saturn, which is a yogakaraka counted from the Moon, flanks the Moon, so he expects the results mostly in Saturn dasa, especially the Venus bhukti (no. 4).

source_views.view: Planets other than the Sun in both the 2nd and 12th from the Moon give Duradhara; the native enjoys pleasures, is charitable, has wealth, vehicles and good servants.
Durudhara: takes life's joys as they come, has abundant wealth and vehicles, is bountiful and served by faithful attendants.

Planets other than the Sun in both the 2nd and 12th; famed for speech, wisdom, valour and virtue, enjoys freedom, comforts, wealth and vehicles, liberal, but suffers from supporting the family. Gives the results of each planet pair. Counts 180 varieties.
Defined as above; 180 varieties, worked out in Sastri's notes (75+70+30+5). Bountiful, wealthy, with vehicles and faithful attendants. The note says the native both earns and spends.
Same definition; per-pair Durudhara results, e.g. Venus and Saturn on either side give a leading man in a traditional clan with much wealth and royal favour.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 4 Dhurdhura Yoga
source_views.view: Planets on either side of the Moon; bountiful, much wealth and conveyances. Each permutation of the five planets gives different results and must be analysed; about 180 varieties. Results in the dasa of the yoga-giving planet.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XX no. 11
source_views.view: Planets in the 2nd and 12th from the Moon: all pleasures, conveyances, liberal and generous, commanding, with dutiful children.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, 11.3.3
source_views.view: Planets other than the Sun in the 2nd and 12th from the Moon; pleasures, charity, wealth, vehicles and good servants.

disagreements: The texts agree on the definition. Saravali adds a cost (grief from supporting family) and gives pair results that are not uniformly good (Mars-Mercury, Mars-Saturn). Raman's Hindu Predictive Astrology adds dutiful children, which the classical verses read here do not give. Srutakirti's rejected variant used the 4th and 10th from the Moon (Brihat Jataka 13.3 notes).
phrasing_guidance: Describe it as a supported, comfortable Moon: resources come in and go out freely. Name the two planets involved, because the pair changes the tone; avoid absolute claims about wealth.

definitions.definition: Planets other than the Sun in both the 2nd and the 12th from the Moon.
Planets other than the Sun in both the 2nd and 12th from the Moon.
Excepting the Sun, planets in both the 2nd and 12th from the Moon.
Planets other than the Sun in both the 2nd and 12th from the Moon; only the five planets Mars to Saturn are used in counting the varieties.

definitions.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 4
definitions.definition: Planets on either side of the Moon (2nd and 12th), drawn from Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus and Saturn.
Planets in both the 4th and 10th from the Moon.

cancellations.condition: Forming planet debilitated or combust, the Moon with Rahu or Ketu, or Rahu in the 10th from the Moon: results mixed

rarity_and_weight: 180 varieties (Brihat Jataka 13.4; Saravali 13.3; Raman no. 4). Raman says the general truth of these lunar yogas is money, power and reputation in varying degrees, and that each permutation produces different results (no. 4).
timing: In the dasas and bhuktis of the flanking planets; in Raman's chart 7, Saturn dasa, especially Venus bhukti (no. 4).

conditional_results.when: manual: if the flanking planets are exalted, in their own or friendly signs, or in such navamsas
manual: if a flanking planet is debilitated or combust, or the Moon is with Rahu or Ketu, or Rahu is in the 10th from the Moon

summary: Kemadruma is the unsupported Moon: no planet other than the Sun in the 2nd or 12th from the Moon (and, in most versions, none with the Moon). It is the classic poverty-and-hardship yoga, but almost every text gives cancellations, chiefly planets in kendras from the lagna or the Moon.
common_outcomes: poverty, sorrow and dependence on others (Raman no. 5; Brihat Jataka 13.6; Phaladeepika 6.7)
loss of learning and intelligence, reproach from others, perils (BPHS 37.11-13)
obscurity even for those of a high-born family (Brihat Jataka 13.6; Phaladeepika 6.7; Saravali 13.7)
having to work hard and succeed through great effort (P.V.R. Narasimha Rao 11.3.4)
rare_outcomes: deprived of food, drink, home, clothing and friends; sickness and grime; living by hard labour (Saravali 13.7)
Raja yogas in the chart fail to work (Jataka Parijata 7.82; Saravali 39.19 when the Moon is also unaspected; enjoylearningsanskrit.com BPHS 37.13)
base or prohibited acts; Raman explains the word neecha in the original as acts against religious, moral and social codes (no. 5)

by_area.personality: sorrowful, mentally as well as physically, per Raman; Saravali says hostile to all (Raman no. 5; Saravali 13.7)
by_area.career: drudging as a menial in the classical idiom; must succeed through great effort (Brihat Jataka 13.6; Rao 11.3.4)
by_area.finance: poverty and penury (BPHS 37.11-13; Raman no. 5; Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XX no. 21: misery and poverty throughout life)
by_area.relationships: deprived of friends; at odds with others (Saravali 13.7)

strengtheners: the Moon unaspected by any planet makes it worse: Saravali counts no aspect as a formation condition and says Raja yogas then lose their existence (Saravali 13.2, 39.19)
Varahamihira: those of royal birth suffer the degradation even more (Raman no. 5 remarks; Brihat Jataka 13.6)
in the Jaimini reading, the Moon's aspect on the malefics makes the effects more severe (BPHS 33.94-99)
weakeners_or_cancellations: any of Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus or Saturn in a kendra from the lagna (Brihat Jataka 13.3 with Garga; Phaladeepika 6.5; BPHS 37.11 as rendered by Santhanam and enjoylearningsanskrit.com)
a planet in a kendra from the Moon (Phaladeepika 6.5; Saravali 13.2; Garga in Brihat Jataka 13.3 notes; Raman no. 5)
the Moon conjoined with a planet other than the Sun (Phaladeepika 6.5; Brihat Jataka 13.3; BPHS 37.11)
the Full Moon aspected by all the planets: long life and freedom from Kemadruma's evils (Saravali 35.47)
a Venus in the 8th destroys a Jaimini-style Kemadruma from the lagna (Rath, Crux, ch. V, chart 30)
lagna_or_context_notes: There are two separate traditions. (1) The lunar Kemadruma: no planet (Sun excluded) in the 2nd or 12th from the Moon. (2) A Jaimini Kemadruma: malefics in the 1st, 2nd and 8th from the Karakamsa, the Arudha lagna or the lagna (BPHS 33.94-99; Rath, Crux, ch. V and ch. XII). Jataka Parijata 7.71 and 7.78-79 also give other Kemadruma-like combinations: the Moon in the 1st or 7th without Jupiter's aspect, Saturn and Venus afflicted in mutual aspect or conjunction, and a weak, waning or debilitated Moon at night with certain aspects.

source_views.view: Excluding the Sun, if no planet is with the Moon or in the 2nd or 12th from it, or in an angle from the ascendant, Kemadruma forms; the native is much reproached, without intelligence or learning, and reduced to poverty and perils.

No planet, excluding the Sun, in the 2nd and 12th from the Moon; a kendra clause excludes the Moon when checking kendras from the lagna. Verse 13: this lunar yoga nullifies the results of other yogas.

Malefics in the Karakamsa, the Arudha lagna and the 2nd and 8th from them give Kemadruma, more severe with the Moon's aspect. It acts in the dasas of the signs or planets concerned, and also when malefics occupy the 2nd and 8th from the running dasa sign or from the chart cast for the start of a dasa.

Kemadruma is the absence of Sunapha, Anapha and Durudhara. Some say it does not exist when a kendra or the Moon is associated with a planet, or when planets occupy a kendra from the Moon. Even those of princely birth become obscure, miserable, low, poor, menial and ill-inclined.

Kemadruma forms when none of the three yogas exists, or the Moon's kendras are empty, or the Moon is unaspected by all planets; extreme difficulty, loss of food, home, clothes and friends, poverty and sickness. A Full Moon aspected by all planets escapes it (35.47). Kemadruma with an unaspected Moon destroys Raja yogas (39.19).

The majority hold that Kemadruma is the absence of the three yogas; others deny it when a kendra from the lagna or the Moon is associated with a planet. Sastri, following Garga, says one of the five planets in any kendra (from the lagna or the Moon) or with the Moon annuls it. The Moon in a kendra with one of the five planets does not by itself destroy it. Effects as in Phaladeepika.

Gives several Kemadruma forms (Moon in the 1st or 7th without Jupiter's aspect; very low ashtakavarga points; afflicted Saturn-Venus; afflicted weak Moon at night). Gives exceptions to the related poverty yogas: the Moon or Venus in a kendra aspected by Jupiter; the Moon with a benefic or between two benefics aspected by Jupiter; the Full Moon in the lagna with a benefic. 7.82: Kemadruma makes Raja yogas vanish like elephants before a lion. 7.83 repeats Brihat Jataka 13.3.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 5 Kemadruma Yoga
source_views.view: No planets on either side of the Moon. Dirty, sorrowful, unrighteous, poor, dependent, a rogue. Some authors cancel it with planets in kendras from the lagna or the Moon or a planet with the Moon; in chart 8 Raman treats the yoga as clearly cancelled because kendras from both the Moon and the lagna are occupied.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XX no. 21
source_views.view: No planets in the 2nd and 12th from the Moon: misery and poverty throughout life; generally capable of neutralising all beneficial yogas.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, 11.3.4
source_views.view: No planets other than the Sun in the 1st, 2nd and 12th from the Moon and no planets other than the Moon in kendras from the lagna. Unlucky, poor, troubled; kills the results of other good yogas, especially Chandra yogas; success comes through great effort.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. V (wealth, charts 29-30) and ch. XII (chart 106)
source_views.view: Uses the Jaimini Kemadruma: malefics including Rahu and Ketu in the 1st, 2nd and 8th from the lagna, Arudha lagna or navamsa lagna. From the lagna it gives lifelong poverty; from the Arudha lagna, a setback such as business collapse or loss of reputation. A benefic (Venus) in the 8th destroys it.

disagreements: The formation rule differs. (a) The bare rule is no planet in the 2nd or 12th from the Moon (Raman; Hindu Predictive Astrology; Phaladeepika and Brihat Jataka 'majority' view). (b) BPHS (Santhanam) and Rao also require no planet with the Moon and none in kendras from the lagna. (c) Saravali also lists empty kendras from the Moon or no aspect on the Moon. Which kendra cancels is also disputed: Brihat Jataka 13.3 says from the lagna; Phaladeepika 6.5 says from the lagna and from the Moon; Garga, cited by Sastri, says either. Sastri rejects reading 'the Moon in a kendra' as a cancellation. Brihat Jataka 13.3 also reports and rejects two variants (4th/10th from the Moon; counting from the Moon's navamsa sign), which Sastri says Parasara accepted. Rahu and Ketu are not counted in the classical lunar rule (Garga's five planets) but are counted as malefics in Rath's Jaimini form. Raman thinks the further kendra-and-navamsa versions are 'not generally acceptable', yet he applies the kendra cancellation in his own chart 8.
phrasing_guidance: Never present it as a sentence of poverty. Check the cancellations first, because most charts with the bare rule have a planet in a kendra. If it stands, describe periods of feeling unsupported and needing to build one's own resources, and pair it with the chart's strengths.

definitions.definition: Excluding the Sun: no planet with the Moon, none in the 2nd or 12th from the Moon, and none in an angle from the ascendant.
No planet (Sun excluded) in the 2nd and 12th from the Moon, with a clause on planets other than the Moon in kendras from the ascendant; the page does not make the link between the clauses explicit.
Absence of Sunapha, Anapha and Durudhara (no planet other than the Sun in the 2nd or 12th from the Moon).
None of the three yogas present, or the kendras from the Moon empty, or the Moon unaspected by all planets.
Absence of the three yogas; with Garga, only Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus and Saturn are counted.
The Moon in the 1st or 7th without the aspect of Jupiter; also weak planets in places with very few ashtakavarga points give Kemadruma-like results.

Afflicted Saturn and Venus in mutual aspect or together; the Moon with a malefic in a malefic sign or navamsa at night aspected by a weak 10th lord; the Moon in its debilitation navamsa with a planet in khala state aspected by the 9th lord; the waning Moon debilitated in a night birth.
Malefics in the Karakamsa, the Arudha lagna and the 2nd and 8th from them.

No planet other than the Sun in the 1st, 2nd or 12th from the Moon, and no planet other than the Moon in a kendra from the lagna.

All planets aspecting the Moon (Saravali: a Full Moon aspected by all planets escapes Kemadruma's ill effects)
cancellations.source: Saravali 35.47; listed among exceptions in Brihat Jataka 13.3 notes

cancellations.condition: For the related poverty yogas: the Moon or Venus in a kendra aspected by Jupiter; the Moon with a benefic or between two benefics aspected by Jupiter; the Moon in a very friendly or exaltation navamsa aspected by Jupiter; the Full Moon in the lagna with a benefic; the exalted Moon in the 10th aspected by Jupiter
Jaimini form: a benefic in the 8th (Venus in Rath's example) destroys the yoga

rarity_and_weight: Weighed heavily when it stands: it is said to nullify Raja yogas and other good yogas (Jataka Parijata 7.82; Saravali 39.19; enjoylearningsanskrit.com BPHS 37.13; Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XX no. 21; Rao 11.3.4). The full uncancelled form is uncommon because the kendra and conjunction exceptions remove most cases; Raman's own illustration (chart 8) is a Kemadruma that is 'distinctly cancelled'.
timing: Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XX no. 21: misery throughout life. BPHS 33.94-99 (Jaimini form): in the dasas of the signs or planets concerned, and whenever malefics are in the 2nd and 8th from the running dasa sign. Rath (Crux ch. XII): from the lagna, lifelong; from the Arudha lagna, a setback in a period.

summary: Shakata (Sakata, 'cart') is the Moon in the 6th, 8th or 12th from Jupiter (equivalently Jupiter in the 12th, 6th or 8th from the Moon). It gives fortune that rises and falls like a cart wheel: luck is lost and regained. Most texts cancel it when the Moon (or Jupiter) is in a kendra from the lagna. A separate Nabhasa Sakata (all planets in the 1st and 7th) shares the name.
common_outcomes: fortune lost and regained repeatedly (Phaladeepika 6.17; Raman no. 12)
being an ordinary, insignificant person in the world (Phaladeepika 6.17; Raman no. 12)
mental grief and unhappiness (Phaladeepika 6.17)
rare_outcomes: poverty, privation and misery; stubbornness; dislike from relatives (Raman no. 12 definition results)
even those of royal family become poor, worn out by trouble, and disliked by the ruler (Jataka Parijata 7.109)
obstacles, turmoil and disease in the dasa of Jupiter when he forms it (Rath, Crux ch. XI)

Nabhasa Sakata (all planets in the 1st and 7th): disease, ugly nails, foolishness, living by pulling carts, poverty, no friends or relatives, a quarrelsome or bad wife (BPHS 35.24; Saravali ch. 21 v. 30; Brihat Jataka 12.13; Raman no. 86)

by_area.career: fortune obstructed now and then (Raman no. 12, citing a Sukra Nadi)
by_area.finance: losses followed by recovery; Raman found the poverty usually nominal in practice (no. 12)
by_area.health: Rath ties it to disease in Jupiter's dasa (Crux ch. XI); the Nabhasa form gives sickness (BPHS 35.24)
by_area.relationships: Nabhasa form: a quarrelsome or bad wife (Raman no. 86; Saravali ch. 21 v. 30)

strengtheners: Rath counts it in the navamsa as well as the rasi; his example has Sakata in both (Crux ch. XI)
weakeners_or_cancellations: the Moon in a kendra from the lagna (Phaladeepika 6.14)
Jupiter, while 6th or 8th from the Moon, in a kendra from the lagna (Jataka Parijata 7.108, Sastri's note)
Raman's experience: the poverty is often only nominal (no. 12)
lagna_or_context_notes: Raman notes that when one planet is 8th from the other, the other is 6th from it, so the 6th/8th pair is symmetrical (no. 12). Raman no. 86 notes that the Nabhasa Sakata can merge with Rajju or Nala yogas for certain lagnas.

source_views.view: The Moon in the 12th, 8th or 6th from Jupiter causes Sakata, but there is no Sakata if the Moon is in a kendra from the lagna. The native often loses his luck and regains it, is ordinary and insignificant, and suffers unavoidable mental grief.

Sakata from the Moon-Jupiter relation. Sastri's note says the yoga loses its bad effects if Jupiter, while in the 6th or 8th from the Moon, is in a kendra from the lagna, and that this differs from Parasara's and Varahamihira's Sakata (all planets in the 1st and 7th). 7.109: even one of royal family becomes indigent, distressed and disliked by the king. The verse text of 7.108 is illegible in the scan; only the translator's note was read.

Only the Nabhasa Sakata: all planets in the ascendant and the 7th. Disease, ugly nails, foolishness, living by pulling carts, poverty, no friends or relatives. Nabhasa yogas act in all dasas (35.50). No Moon-Jupiter Sakata was found in the Santhanam chapters read.
Nabhasa Sakata: all seven planets in the 1st and 7th. Livelihood by driving a cart, sickly, a bad wife. Sastri's note says the effect is bad because the planets are in opposition.
Nabhasa Sakata: all planets only in the ascendant and the 7th. Diseases, a bad wife, dullness, living by pulling carts, poverty, no relatives or friends.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 12 Sakata Yoga
source_views.view: The Moon in the 12th, 6th or 8th from Jupiter. Loss and regaining of fortune, ordinariness, poverty, stubbornness, dislike from relatives. Raman notes that Parasara and Varahamihira define Sakata as all planets in the 1st and 7th. In many horoscopes he found the poverty only nominal. A Sukra Nadi says fortune is obstructed now and then, whenever the Moon transits the 6th, 8th or 12th from natal Jupiter.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 86 (Nabhasa)
source_views.view: All planets in the lagna and 7th: poverty and an unhappy domestic life, manual labour, sickness, a quarrelsome wife; evil because the 1st and 7th become the focus.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. XI (disease)
source_views.view: Jupiter in the 6th, 8th or 12th from the Moon causes Sakata (obstacles, turmoil, disease). His example has it in both the rasi and the navamsa, and knee trouble started with Jupiter dasa.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, 11.5 (Nabhasa yogas)
source_views.view: Lists only the Nabhasa Sakata: all planets in the 1st and 7th from the lagna; disease, ugly nails, foolishness, no friends or family, living by pulling carts.

disagreements: Two different yogas share the name. BPHS, Brihat Jataka, Saravali and Rao give only the Nabhasa Sakata (all planets in the 1st and 7th). Phaladeepika, Jataka Parijata, Raman and Rath give the Moon-Jupiter Sakata. Within the Moon-Jupiter form: Phaladeepika and Raman use the Moon in the 6th, 8th or 12th from Jupiter. Jataka Parijata (per Sastri's note) speaks of Jupiter in the 6th or 8th from the Moon. Rath uses Jupiter in the 6th, 8th or 12th from the Moon. Jupiter 12th from the Moon is the same as the Moon 2nd from Jupiter, not 12th, so the '12th' clauses of Raman and Rath do not describe the same configuration. On cancellation, Phaladeepika uses the Moon in a kendra from the lagna; Jataka Parijata's note uses Jupiter in a kendra from the lagna. Raman doubts the severity in practice.
phrasing_guidance: Describe ups and downs in fortune that recover, not lasting poverty. Check the kendra cancellation first, and say which version (Moon-Jupiter or all planets in the 1st and 7th) the calculator found.

definitions.definition: The Moon in the 12th, 8th or 6th from Jupiter.

definitions.source: Jataka Parijata 7.108 (Sastri's note; verse illegible in scan)
definitions.definition: Jupiter in the 6th or 8th from the Moon.

definitions.definition: The Moon in the 12th, 6th or 8th from Jupiter.
Jupiter in the 6th, 8th or 12th from the Moon; applied in the navamsa too.

definitions.source: BPHS 35.11; Brihat Jataka 12.4; Saravali ch. 21 v. 15; Raman no. 86; Rao 11.5 (Nabhasa Sakata)
definitions.definition: All seven planets (nodes omitted, per Raman) in the lagna and the 7th.

cancellations.condition: The Moon in a kendra from the lagna
Jupiter (while 6th or 8th from the Moon) in a kendra from the lagna

rarity_and_weight: The Moon-Jupiter form is common, since it needs only a sign relation between two bodies. Raman gives it modest weight: in many charts the poverty was nominal and fortune was only obstructed at times (no. 12). The Nabhasa form, needing all planets in two signs, is rare. Nabhasa yogas act throughout life (BPHS 35.50).
timing: Raman, citing a Sukra Nadi: the effects come each time the Moon transits the 6th, 8th or 12th from natal Jupiter (no. 12). Rath: in Jupiter's dasa (Crux ch. XI). Nabhasa form: in all dasas (BPHS 35.50; Brihat Jataka ch. 12 notes).

summary: Shubha Kartari forms when benefics occupy both the 12th and the 2nd from the lagna, 'hemming' the ascendant between benefics. The texts give long life, health, fearlessness, wealth and good character. The principle applies to any house or planet.
common_outcomes: long life, fearlessness, freedom from disease and enemies, happiness and wealth (Phaladeepika 6.11)
eloquence, charm and virtue (BPHS 36.1-2, Subha yoga)
superior lustre, wealth and strength (Jataka Parijata 7.127)
rare_outcomes: Santhanam's note adds a happy life, health, wealth, longevity and fame, saying the text does not state these (BPHS 36.1-2 notes)

by_area.personality: eloquent, charming, virtuous, fearless (BPHS 36.2; Phaladeepika 6.11; Rao 11.6)

strengtheners: a benefic in the lagna as well as in the 2nd and 12th: Santhanam calls it a Subha yoga of a very great order (BPHS 36.1-2 notes)
benefics unaspected by malefics (Phaladeepika 6.8, for the related Susubha yoga, a benefic in the 2nd)
weakeners_or_cancellations: functional malefice of the flanking benefics: Santhanam's example of Aquarius lagna with Mercury in the 2nd and Jupiter in the 12th, which he calls worse than a typical Asubha yoga (BPHS 36.1-2 notes)
the dignity, strength and associations of the planets can override the yoga (BPHS 36.1-2 notes)
lagna_or_context_notes: Santhanam warns against judging by natural benefic or malefic status alone: for Aquarius lagna, Mercury (lord of the 5th and 8th) in the 2nd and Jupiter (lord of the 2nd and 11th) in the 12th do not give a good result (BPHS 36.1-2 notes). Rao and Rath apply Kartari to any house, arudha or planet (Rao 11.6 footnote; Crux ch. VIII, X).

source_views.view: Benefics in the 12th and 2nd from the lagna give Subhakartari: long-lived, fearless, free from disease and enemies, happy and rich. Its effects follow those of benefic-made yogas like Sunapha (6.13).

A benefic in the ascendant, or benefics in both the 12th and 2nd, give Subha yoga: eloquent, charming and virtuous. Santhanam's notes say the double-flank form is superior and that dignity and house rulership must be weighed.
Renders the clause as benefics in the 2nd or 12th house making the yoga auspicious.
Benefics in the 12th and 2nd from the lagna give Soumyakartari (Subhakartari): superior lustre, wealth and strength. Sastri's note says the Sun and the Moon are not counted in these yogas.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, 11.6 and footnote 31
source_views.view: Subha yoga: benefics in the lagna or subha kartari (benefics in the 12th and 2nd); eloquence, good looks and character. Kartari means scissors; subha kartari on any house helps its matters and can be seen for any house or planet.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XI (Seventh House), chart 23
source_views.view: Applies subhakartari to a house: in chart 23 the 7th house (occupied by malefics) is subject to subhakartari caused by Mercury on one side and Venus and the Moon on the other, so Raman counts the Moon as a benefic for kartari.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. VIII (fifth house) and ch. X (seventh house)
source_views.view: Uses subhakartari on houses and arudhas; a house can be under both subha and papa kartari at once; the seventh house under subhakartari brings the yoga's effects into its matters.

disagreements: BPHS (Santhanam) and Phaladeepika require benefics in both the 2nd and 12th; the enjoylearningsanskrit.com rendering of BPHS 36.1 reads '2nd or 12th'. BPHS treats a benefic in the lagna itself as a Subha yoga as well. Jataka Parijata (Sastri's note) excludes the Sun and the Moon from the count, whereas Raman counts the Moon as one of the benefics forming subhakartari (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XI, chart 23). Santhanam's notes say functional rulership can override natural benefic status.
phrasing_guidance: Describe it as a protected, supported self: health, poise and goodwill. Check the house rulership of the flanking benefics before calling it strong.

definitions.definition: The 12th and 2nd from the lagna occupied by benefics.
Benefics in both the 12th and 2nd (Subha yoga; a benefic in the lagna also forms Subha yoga).
Benefics in the 2nd or 12th house (Subha yoga).
Benefics in the 12th and 2nd from the lagna; the Sun and Moon are not reckoned.
Benefics in the 12th and 2nd from a house (here the lagna); applicable to any house or planet.

cancellations.condition: The flanking benefics are functional malefics for the lagna (e.g. Aquarius lagna with Mercury in the 2nd and Jupiter in the 12th): judged worse than a typical Asubha yoga
Dignity, strength and relations of the planets may nullify or limit the yoga

rarity_and_weight: Santhanam ranks the double-flank form above a single benefic in the lagna, and a benefic in all three houses as a Subha yoga of a very great order (BPHS 36.1-2 notes). He also says the extra benefits will not fully mature from a single ordinary benefic.

conditional_results.when: manual: if the benefics in the 2nd and 12th rule dusthanas or are otherwise functional malefics for the lagna
effects: the expected good results do not come

summary: Papa Kartari forms when malefics occupy both the 12th and the 2nd from the lagna, hemming the ascendant between malefics like the blades of scissors. The texts give poverty, unhappiness, sinful tendencies, harm to health and longevity, and loss of spouse or children. The same principle is applied to any house, lord or significator.
common_outcomes: poverty, impurity, unhappiness, loss of wife and children, damage to a limb and short life (Phaladeepika 6.11)
sensuality, sinful acts and enjoying others' wealth (BPHS 36.1-2, Asubha yoga)
criminal tendencies, living on begged food, impurity (Jataka Parijata 7.127)
rare_outcomes: defeat, bondage and loss of reputation when Saturn and Rahu cause it on the lagna (Rath, Crux ch. IV)
applied to the 7th house and its lord without benefic influence: loss of husband (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XI)
[maraka: Moon in the lagna hemmed between malefics without benefic aspect is listed among balarishta (infant death) combinations] (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XII; Saravali 10.35-36)

by_area.personality: lustful, sinful, deceitful per the texts (BPHS 36.2; Jataka Parijata 7.126)
by_area.career: loss of reputation; defeat (Rath, Crux ch. IV)
by_area.finance: poor; living on others' wealth or begged food (Phaladeepika 6.11; BPHS 36.2; Jataka Parijata 7.127)
by_area.health: damage to a limb, short life (Phaladeepika 6.11); two or three malefics harm health and longevity (BPHS 36.1-2 notes)
by_area.relationships: bereft of wife (Phaladeepika 6.11); for the 7th house, loss of spouse (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XI)

strengtheners: more malefics make it worse: one malefic may not give such bad results, but two or three do (BPHS 36.1-2 notes)
no benefic influence on the hemmed house or planet (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XI; Uttara Kalamrita, rule on hemmed bhava, lord and karaka)
weakeners_or_cancellations: well-dignified malefics: Santhanam's example of Virgo lagna with exalted Saturn in the 2nd and the Sun in Leo in the 12th need not be called Asubha (BPHS 36.1-2 notes)

the hemming malefics being the significators (lords) of the very house concerned: Raman says papakartari on Venus is toned down because the Sun and Saturn hemming it are the lords of the lagna and of the 7th from the Moon (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XI)
lagna_or_context_notes: Raman, Rao and Rath apply papakartari to any house, lord or karaka, not only the lagna (How to Judge a Horoscope vols. 1-2; Rao 11.6 footnote 31; Crux passim). Uttara Kalamrita says a bhava is destroyed when the bhava, its lord and its karaka are all hemmed between malefics, joined by weak malefics, and without benefic aspect or conjunction.

source_views.view: Malefics in the 12th and 2nd from the lagna give Papakartari: poor, impure, unhappy, without wife and children, deprived of some limb, short-lived. Malefic-made yogas give the opposite of Sunapha-type benefits (6.13).

A malefic in the ascendant, or malefics in both the 12th and 2nd, cause Asubha yoga: sensuous, sinful, enjoys others' wealth. The notes say severity rises with the number of malefics, health and longevity suffer, and well-dignified malefics may prove favourable.
Malefics in the 12th and 2nd from the lagna give Papakartari: criminal, eating begged food, impure. The note says the Sun and the Moon are not counted.

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita (tr. P.S. Sastri), rule on destruction of a bhava (ch. on effects of planets and houses)
source_views.view: When a bhava, its lord and its karaka are hemmed between malefics, joined by weak malefics and without benefic aspect or conjunction, the bhava is destroyed.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. 4 (First House, Cancer illustration); vol. 2, ch. XI (Seventh House)
source_views.view: Defines papakartari as hemmed in between malefic planets and applies it to the lagna lord (Moon between Saturn and Ketu) and to the 7th house and its lord: without benefic influence it shows loss of husband.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, 11.6 and footnote 31
source_views.view: Asubha yoga: malefics in the lagna or paapa kartari on it; many desires, sinful, enjoys others' wealth. Paapa kartari harms the matters of any house it falls on.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. IV (ascendant, Nehru's chart) and passim
source_views.view: Saturn and Rahu causing papakartari on the lagna indicate defeat, bondage and loss of reputation. Rahu is counted as a malefic in forming it.

disagreements: Which malefics count is not settled. Jataka Parijata's translator excludes the Sun and Moon. Raman counts Ketu (Saturn and Ketu hemming) and Rath counts Rahu, while the classical verses say only 'malefics'. BPHS includes a malefic in the lagna itself under Asubha yoga. Santhanam's notes say dignified malefics may help rather than harm. The enjoylearningsanskrit.com rendering of BPHS 36.1 has '2nd or 12th' for the benefic clause, while Santhanam has both.
phrasing_guidance: Describe pressure or constraint on health, confidence and resources that needs care, not doom. Do not repeat short-life or spouse-loss lines; check the dignity of the malefics and any benefic aspect on the lagna first.

definitions.definition: The 12th and 2nd from the lagna occupied by malefics.
Malefics in both the 12th and 2nd (Asubha yoga; a malefic in the lagna also forms Asubha yoga).
Malefics in the 12th and 2nd from the lagna; the Sun and Moon are not reckoned.

definitions.source: Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XI
definitions.definition: A house or planet hemmed in between malefic planets.
Malefics in the 12th and 2nd from a house; applies to any house or planet.

cancellations.condition: The flanking malefics are strong and well dignified (e.g. Virgo lagna, exalted Saturn in the 2nd, the Sun in own sign Leo in the 12th): need not be called Asubha
Benefic aspect on or association with the hemmed house or planet reduces it (the bhava is destroyed only when there is no benefic aspect or conjunction)
cancellations.source: Uttara Kalamrita (rule on destruction of a bhava); Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XI (without any benefic influence)

cancellations.condition: The hemming malefics are themselves the lords or significators of the house concerned: papakartari is toned down
cancellations.source: Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XI

rarity_and_weight: Severity scales with the number of malefics: a single malefic may not give such bad results, but two or three do (BPHS 36.1-2 notes). Raman weighs it together with the other afflictions of the house (How to Judge a Horoscope).

conditional_results.when: manual: if the hemming malefics are exalted or in their own signs
effects: need not be treated as Asubha; may prove favourable

conditional_results.when: manual: if the lagna or its lord receives no benefic aspect or conjunction
effects: the full harm of the hemming
conditional_results.source: Uttara Kalamrita; Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XI

summary: 'Grahan' (eclipse) yoga, the Sun or the Moon conjoined with Rahu or Ketu, is a later, popular name; the classical texts read here do not define a yoga by that name. They do treat birth at an actual eclipse as inauspicious and needing remedy. They also treat the Moon 'seized' by Rahu or Ketu as spoiling lunar yogas and pointing to poverty when malefics aspect it. Modern authors read the node-luminary conjunction as an eclipse of that light, with obstructed or transformed results.
themes: obstruction of Sun or Moon significations
common_outcomes: birth at a solar or lunar eclipse brings ailments, distress and poverty, and the text prescribes remedial rites (BPHS 91.1-14)
the Moon with Rahu or Ketu makes the results of the lunar yogas mixed (Jataka Parijata 7.107)
the Moon seized by Rahu or Ketu and aspected by a malefic: early poverty (Jataka Parijata 7.75)
the planet joined with a node is eclipsed: its energy is obstructed, negated or released (Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, 'The Lunar Nodes')
rare_outcomes: the Moon aspected by a benefic that has lost a planetary war, and seized by a node in an eclipse: the native is indigent (Jataka Parijata 7.76)
Rahu eclipsing the Sun (Sun in the 6th context): torment by disease; the evil is overcome if the Sun's longitude is higher than Rahu's and worse if lower (Rath, Crux ch. IX 9.2)
a close Sun-Rahu conjunction can show deep spirituality or renunciation, depending on the arudha lagna (Rath, Crux ch. XV)
the Sun-Rahu 'eclipse combination' can produce either a short-lived saint or a long-lived criminal (Rath, Crux ch. XII)

[maraka: text predicts danger to life / death] eclipsed Moon (or Sun at a solar eclipse) in the lagna with malefics and Mars in the 8th: death of mother and child (Saravali 10.37-38; Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XII balarishta no. 6, with Saturn)

[maraka: text predicts danger to life / death] birth during a solar or lunar eclipse: death of the father or the mother respectively (Uttara Kalamrita 8.8); BPHS 91.1-14 also names danger of death among the effects of eclipse birth
[maraka: text predicts danger to life / death] the Moon with Rahu and another malefic, Mars in the 8th: death of mother and child (Jataka Parijata 4.36)

by_area.personality: the Moon is the mind; Rath reads Moon with Ketu as an eclipse of the mind in a disease context (Crux ch. XI)
by_area.finance: poverty when the node-seized Moon is aspected by malefics (Jataka Parijata 7.75-76); poverty among the effects of eclipse birth (BPHS 91.1-14)
by_area.health: ailments (BPHS 91.1-14); torment by disease when Rahu eclipses the Sun (Rath, Crux ch. IX)
by_area.family: eclipse birth threatens the father (solar) or mother (lunar) in Uttara Kalamrita 8.8
by_area.spirituality: Sun-Rahu close conjunction may give renunciation or great spirituality (Rath, Crux ch. XV); Frawley calls eclipses points of energy transformation

strengtheners: a malefic aspect on the node-seized Moon (Jataka Parijata 7.75)
an actual eclipse at birth, not only a sign conjunction (BPHS ch. 91; Uttara Kalamrita 8.8)
the Sun at a lower longitude than Rahu (Rath, Crux ch. IX)
weakeners_or_cancellations: the Sun at a higher longitude than Rahu: the evil is overcome (Rath, Crux ch. IX)
remedial rites for eclipse birth are said to wipe off the evil effects (BPHS 91.1-14)
lagna_or_context_notes: Rath reads the Sun-Rahu result through the arudha lagna: in Aquarius the native is spiritual, in Leo the reverse (Crux ch. XV).

source_views.source: BPHS 91.1-14 (tr. Santhanam vol. 2, 'Remedies from Birth in Eclipses')
source_views.view: Birth at a solar or lunar eclipse brings ailments, distress, poverty and danger of death. The remedy is worship of the nakshatra deity, the Sun (solar) or Moon (lunar), and Rahu with specified images, offerings, havana and feeding of Brahmins, which wipes off the evil.

The Moon seized by Rahu or Ketu and aspected by a malefic gives poverty. The Moon aspected by a war-defeated benefic and seized by a node in an eclipse gives indigence. The Moon with Rahu or Ketu, or Rahu 10th from the Moon, makes lunar yoga results mixed. In his note to 4.36-37 (arishta) Sastri says the 'grasped Moon' (grasta Chandra) is read as the Moon in association with Rahu, not necessarily an actual eclipse; 4.36 itself says the Moon with Rahu and another malefic, with Mars in the 8th, kills mother and child [maraka].
Eclipsed Moon in the lagna with malefics and Mars in the 8th: the child dies with the mother; similarly for a solar eclipse with the Sun and malefics in the lagna. [maraka]
If birth (or a girl's first menses) occurs during a solar or lunar eclipse, the father or the mother respectively dies. [maraka]

source_views.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, 'The Lunar Nodes'
source_views.view: The nodes are the eclipse points and mythically swallow the luminaries, so they can overpower the Sun and Moon. Any planet joined with a node is a kind of eclipse of that planet, its energy obstructed, negated or liberated. Eclipses are points of energy transformation.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. IX (9.2), ch. XII, ch. XV
source_views.view: Rahu eclipsing the Sun gives torment by disease, overcome if the Sun is ahead of Rahu in longitude. A Sun-Rahu eclipse combination can give a short-lived saint or a long-lived criminal. A close Sun-Rahu conjunction can show great spirituality and renunciation in Rahu dasa when the arudha lagna supports it.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XII (Eighth House, Balarishta no. 6)
source_views.view: If the eclipsed Moon joins Saturn in the lagna and Mars is in the 8th, both mother and child die. [maraka]

disagreements: Provenance: none of the classical texts read (BPHS, Phaladeepika, Saravali, Brihat Jataka, Jataka Parijata, Uttara Kalamrita) names a 'Grahan yoga'. The term appears to be later or popular usage; its first appearance was not found. The classical material either requires an actual eclipse at birth (BPHS 91; Uttara Kalamrita 8.8; Saravali 10.37-38) or speaks of the Moon 'seized' by a node, which Sastri reads as simple association with Rahu (Jataka Parijata 4.36-37 notes). The calculator's rule (Sun or Moon with Rahu or Ketu in the same sign) is broader than an actual eclipse. Modern authors split on tone: Frawley and Rath allow spiritual or transformative results, while the classical lines are uniformly adverse.
phrasing_guidance: Say that this is a modern label, and that a same-sign conjunction is not an actual eclipse at birth. Describe it as pressure or intensity on the Sun's or Moon's matters (vitality, father, mind, mother) that can also turn inward or spiritual. Never repeat the parent-death or infant-death lines to a user.

definitions.source: Calculator / popular usage (no classical source found)
definitions.definition: The Sun or the Moon in the same sign as Rahu or Ketu.
Birth during an actual solar or lunar eclipse (not a yoga by name).
The Moon 'seized by' or in conjunction with Rahu or Ketu.
Any planet conjoined with a lunar node is a kind of eclipse of that planet.
The 'grasped Moon' read as the Moon in association with Rahu, not necessarily an actual eclipse.

cancellations.condition: The Sun has a higher longitude than Rahu: the evil (disease) is overcome
Remedial rites for eclipse birth remove the evil effects

rarity_and_weight: The sign-conjunction form is fairly common. The texts give heavy weight only to an actual eclipse at birth (BPHS ch. 91; Uttara Kalamrita 8.8; Saravali 10.37-38). For the conjunction, Jataka Parijata 7.107 treats it as a modifier that mixes the lunar yogas rather than as a yoga by itself.
timing: Rath: in Rahu dasa (renunciation in his ch. XV example; the mother's sudden death in a Rahu dasa in his ch. XII example).

remedies.remedy: for birth at an eclipse: install images of the eclipse nakshatra's deity (gold), the Sun (gold) for a solar or the Moon (silver) for a lunar eclipse, and Rahu (lead); worship them with the matching mantras, flowers and cloth; perform havana with arka wood for the Sun, palasa for the Moon, durva grass for Rahu and pipal for the nakshatra deity; sprinkle the child and parents with kalasha water, honour the priest and feed Brahmins

conditional_results.when: manual: if the Moon joined by Rahu or Ketu is aspected by a malefic
manual: if the Moon is with Rahu or Ketu while a lunar yoga (Sunapha, Anapha, Durudhara) is present
effects: the lunar yoga gives mixed results

conditional_results.when: manual: if Rahu is conjoined with the Sun and the Sun's longitude is lower than Rahu's
manual: if Rahu is conjoined with the Sun and the Sun's longitude is higher than Rahu's
